item.title: Note 7
item.description:
Notes No. 7
Uncertainty in a measured win rate: SE = √(p(1 − p) / n). 100 trades at a 50% win rate: SE = 5 points. The 95% interval runs from about 40% to 60%.
A win rate measured over a sample of trades is an estimate, and its standard error is the square root of p(1 − p) / n, where p is the observed win rate and n the number of trades. With 100 trades and a 50% win rate the standard error is 0.05, or 5 percentage points. An approximate 95% interval is the estimate plus or minus 1.96 standard errors, here about 40% to 60%. Because n sits under a square root, four times as many trades are needed to halve the uncertainty: 400 trades narrow the same interval to about 45% to 55%.
Notes from my trading. Not investment advice.
